picks.title: New Game Uses Local AI Model Trained Entirely on Studio's Own Artists
picks.excerpt: Studio Atelico built more than 10 prototypes around a local, on-device model trained only on its own artists' work. The takeaways: authored constraints, artist consent, statistical testing, and tighter creative-technical collaboration.
picks.rationale: A working answer to the consent problem — train small on your own art, keep inference on-device — which turns generative art from a legal risk into a studio asset.

picks.title: Create Procedural UE5 Animations Based on Music with Vizibeat
picks.excerpt: Vizibeat is an Unreal Engine plug-in that drives procedural animation directly from an audio track, producing motion without any keyframing.
picks.rationale: A concrete tool an animator can install tomorrow: signal-driven procedural motion that stays fully editable in-engine, unlike generative video.

picks.title: The Witcher 4 dev is "still predominantly using people" over AI in development, says CEO
picks.excerpt: CD Projekt Red's CEO says the studio still leans on people rather than AI for The Witcher 4, while conceding that every studio has to make its own judgment call.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the clearest public statement yet of where a flagship RPG studio is putting its craft budget.

picks.title: Roblox makes three of its AI safety tools open source
picks.excerpt: Roblox released three of its AI moderation and safety models as open source, via the Robust Open Online Safety Tools community it co-founded with Google, OpenAI, and Discord.
picks.rationale: Downloadable models, not a policy statement — smaller creator platforms can inherit a safety layer that used to be a design constraint they had to build alone.

picks.title: Nvidia tech behind PUBG's genAI team mates will let folks chat to creature-collecting RPG Aniimo's not-Pokemon next year
picks.excerpt: Nvidia ACE, the tech that powered PUBG's generative AI teammates, is heading into Aniimo, where players will be able to talk to the creatures they collect from early 2027.
picks.rationale: ACE moves from tech demo to a shipping creature-collector, turning the design question from 'can NPCs talk' into 'what should a talking companion be allowed to say'.
